items_missed: No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation — jumped straight from 'how can I help' into pulling up the account
Never asked the moving-stressor question ('anything you're particularly worried about?')
Packing pricing given as 'same hourly rate' with no mention of materials cost
Never stated the number of movers or trucks — quoted $204/hr with no crew size attached
No estimate variables explained — stairs/elevator, walk distance, packing time, and specialty items were all probed but never tied to how they could move the time or the bill
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech missing — customer volunteered he was hauling small items himself all week, which was a wide-open door for the consolidation/'take a carload' tip
Confirmation email described but no BOLDED-details-at-top and no 'reply with any corrections' verification ask
No business hours given — only 'feel free to give us a call'
Never used the customer's name once in 13 minutes — 'sir' every time
No Ecobox/Sparefoot referral even though the customer was actively sourcing boxes and asked whether movers bring them
Insurance explained as $2,000 coverage only — no 60¢/lb baseline contrast
top_strength: The discovery was genuinely thorough — origin and destination addresses, unit number, floor, elevator vs. stairs, parking spot and walk distance at BOTH ends, patio/garage items, heavy and fragile items, appliances, and box count. He also handled the TV-remount question at the end accurately and without overpromising.
coaching_note: Arden burned roughly five minutes of a thirteen-minute call re-explaining wrapping vs. packing, and the customer STILL asked at the end whether movers bring the fifteen boxes. Give the distinction once, cleanly and up front ('wrapping your furniture is included in the rate; packing means we put your small items into boxes you provide — do you want that?'), then move on. The time he saved there is exactly what's missing at the back half of the call, where he skipped Save Your Ass entirely — and this customer had already told him he was carloading small items himself all week, which is the single best setup for that speech you will get.
phone_presence_notes: Polite but mechanical and mildly impatient — 'So, do you need packing sir or no?', repeated 'sorry, go ahead sir', zero use of the customer's name, and no acknowledgment of the customer's obvious confusion beyond restating the same script.
audio_review_reason: Score of 2 — want to confirm the flatness and the clipped packing exchange are actually tone and not just a rough transcript with heavy cross-talk.
